One runway, several rulebooks: SNT-TC-1A, NAS 410 and San Antonio NDT careers

Most of San Antonio's aviation NDT happens along a single runway. Kelly Field, the industrial airport at Port San Antonio on the former Kelly Air Force Base, shares its runway with Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland. Boeing runs a maintenance and modification center for large aircraft there, with programs that include the C-17 Globemaster III, the Navy's F/A-18 and the government's executive fleet. StandardAero does commercial and military engine overhaul, Chromalloy repairs engine components, and Knight Aerospace builds cargo-aircraft medical modules and interiors. East and south of the city, a refinery in Valero's headquarters town, the Eagle Ford Shale and the power fleet hire technicians under industrial codes. A San Antonio career can cross between these worlds, but a certification never crosses with it.

Engine overhaul and component repair at the Port

Engine and component shops often work two ways at once. As repair stations they follow the personnel standard named in their own manuals and customer contracts; FAA advisory circular AC 65-31B accepts NAS 410, ATA Specification 105, SNT-TC-1A, EN 4179 and others, and the FAA itself certifies no NDT personnel. As suppliers to engine makers and defense customers, they often find NAS 410 written into purchase orders. Either way, the employer's Level 3, a designated Responsible Level 3 where NAS 410 applies, decides what earlier training and experience to credit. Fluorescent penetrant, eddy current and ultrasonic inspection of rotating parts make up much of the work.

Military airframe work done under contract

Contractor maintenance on military aircraft follows the NDT clauses in the contract. Defense aerospace contracts commonly flow NAS 410 down from the prime, a carry-over from its replacement of MIL-STD-410, though a contract can name a service-specific requirement instead, so ask the program's Level 3 which document governs before assuming. Uniformed NDI technicians on the JBSA installations work under their service's own technical orders and personnel rules.

From military NDI to a civilian certification

Service members leaving Lackland, Randolph or other bases with NDI experience often ask how it converts. It converts as evidence, not as a certificate. Collect your training records with course content and hours, a signed record of experience by method, and any examination results, then put them in front of the new employer's Level III or RL3. A NAS 410 shop at Port San Antonio may credit part of that record and set gap training and examinations; a refinery contractor certifying under SNT-TC-1A will run the same review against its own written practice. NAS 410 shops usually look hardest at formal penetrant and magnetic particle hours, where the aerospace standard asks for more than SNT-TC-1A recommends.

Refinery, Eagle Ford and South Texas Project work

The east-side refinery inspects under API 510, 570 and 653 programs with NDT to ASME Section V. Eagle Ford gathering lines and gas plants follow API 1104 and ASME B31.3. Outage work at the South Texas Project, which CPS Energy co-owns, follows ASME Section XI, which looks to CP-189 for personnel. Contractors on this side certify under written practices built on SNT-TC-1A, or CP-189 for nuclear work. A UT Level II from the Eagle Ford counts as evidence at a Port San Antonio tenant, not as an aerospace certification.

For Port San Antonio tenants and their suppliers

Shops holding aviation and industrial work should print the standard and revision on each certification, keep training records to the NAS 410 standard of evidence, apply the stricter vision rule where the two documents differ, and agree the move to NAS 410 Revision 6, released in December 2025, with their customers. NAS 410 audit documentation support prepares and checks the files your RL3 signs off, and aviation NDT consulting covers written practices built on SNT-TC-1A, procedures and outside agency ASNT Level III services.

Atlantis and San Antonio

Atlantis training follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A: self-paced online theory, Q&A with our ASNT NDT Level III (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT), practice in the Practical NDT hangar, and the hands-on practical at your employer's facility. There is no Atlantis classroom in San Antonio. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 to San Antonio employers or veterans. If your target employer runs a NAS 410 program, its RL3 decides whether outside coursework will count, so ask before enrolling. Read NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A for the full comparison, aviation NDT training in San Antonio for local hangar methods, and eddy current testing training for the method engine shops use most.
